data.name: Moutamid
data.gender_notes: Moutamid is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root ‘t-m-d’, meaning ‘to be firm, steadfast, or secure’. In Islamic history, Moutamid was the name of several prominent figures, including a medieval ruler of Seville, Spain. The name Moutamid carries the meaning “Firm, Steadfast” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Moutamid usually hope their child will grow to embody firm, steadfast and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of unwavering faith and determination.
data.etymology: Moutamid belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Firm, Steadfast.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Moutamid total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Moutamid was an influential Islamic ruler who reigned over the Umayyad Caliphate of al-Andalus from 822 to 851 CE. During his reign, he successfully defended the territory against various Christian and Berber invasions, making him an essential figure in preserving Islamic rule in Spain. Today, his name is associated with resilience and strength in the face of adversity, inspiring generations of Muslims in Spain and beyond.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, the name Moutamid holds spiritual significance beyond its historical and cultural import. By bearing this name, one could be reminded of the importance of steadfastness and patience in their daily life. The name evokes the Prophet's hadith, "Indeed, the strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, although we all continue to be rewarded," (Sahih Muslim). This reminder can inspire a deep sense of commitment and unwavering faith in Allah, with the hope of attaining His pleasure and blessings.
